findings.claim: The unit is presented as Chemistry Paper 2, and all eight lessons sit in it.
findings.truth: Paper 2 assesses topic 1 plus topics 6-9. Four lessons are wholly or partly Paper 1. L2 (reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier, Haber, fertilisers) is topics 4.13-4.17 and 5.19C-5.24C, both Paper 1. The chromatography half of L4 (paper chromatography, Rf values) is 2.9-2.11, Paper 1; the ion and gas tests in the same lesson are 9.1C-9.9C and are correctly Paper 2. L8 is almost entirely Paper 1 or out of scope: potable water and desalination are 2.12, recycling metals is 4.10, life-cycle assessment is 4.11-4.12, and reverse osmosis and the four-stage sewage works appear nowhere in this specification. In L7 the explanation of why alloys are harder is 5.5C (Paper 1); nanoparticles, glass, ceramics and composites (9.35C-9.39C) are correctly Paper 2. Coverage gaps for this paper: topic 6 (Groups 1, 7 and 0, statements 6.1-6.16) is absent altogether, including the chlorine test at 6.8 which the unit teaches only as a gas test; the energy half of topic 7 (7.9-7.16: exothermic and endothermic changes, bond-energy calculations, reaction profiles) is absent; 8.14 (hydrogen versus petrol as a car fuel) and 9.25C (DNA, starch and protein polymers) are absent; and core practical 9.6C (identify the ions in unknown salts) is taught in L4 without being named as a core practical. No lesson claims a paper number in its text, so nothing needed correcting in prose. Options: (a) move L2 and L8 into the Paper 1 unit and split the chromatography half out of L4; (b) leave the lessons where they are and add two new lessons for topic 6 and for energy changes; (c) leave as built and accept the mismatch. Recommendation: (b) plus a later move of L2, because topic 6 and the energy changes carry roughly a quarter of this paper and no lesson teaches them.
findings.evidence: spec 1CH0 assessment overview, Paper 1 and Paper 2 content lists; statements 2.9-2.12, 4.10-4.17, 5.5C, 5.19C-5.24C, 6.1-6.16, 7.9-7.16, 8.14, 9.1C-9.39C

findings.claim: L6 and L7 carry tier 'higher' in the lessons table, and both wrap their whole article in a higher-only block.
findings.truth: Nothing in L7 is bold in the specification (9.35C-9.39C), and in L6 only 9.22C (polyesters as condensation polymers) is bold. The wrappers are fixed in _edits.json, but the tier field is lesson metadata that an edit cannot reach. Recommendation: set both lessons to tier 'both'. Otherwise Foundation students lose alkenes, addition polymers, alcohols, fermentation, carboxylic acids, nanoparticles, glass, ceramics and composites, which are all examinable at Foundation.
findings.evidence: spec statements 9.10C-9.21C, 9.23C-9.24C, 9.26C-9.39C are not bold; 9.22C is bold

findings.claim: L1 description is exactly 100 characters; L7 is 103; L8 is 107.
findings.truth: The house validator needs a description under 100 characters. All three shortened without losing meaning.

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper covers dynamic equilibrium, the whole Haber process and the fertilisers section.
findings.truth: None of that content is bold. Dynamic equilibrium is 4.14, the Haber reaction and its conditions are 4.15, 4.16 and 5.19C, and fertilisers are 5.22C-5.24C. This is the known build fault: the wrapper was used to mean separate-science only, and in a separate-science course that hides Foundation content. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 4.14, 4.15, 4.16, 5.19C, 5.22C-5.24C are not bold in chemistry-1CH0-bold.md

findings.claim: The Higher-tier content in L2 carried no tier signal once the blanket wrapper was wrong.
findings.truth: Predicting how the position of equilibrium shifts is bold at 4.17, and relating industrial conditions to yield and rate is bold at 5.20C and 5.21C. A narrow higher-only wrapper now covers the Le Chatelier section and the 450 degrees / 200 atmospheres compromise, and the two practice questions, three knowledge checks and three flashcards that test those statements are tagged (Higher tier).

findings.claim: L3 question 6 and L5 question 5 are typed '9 marks - Evaluate'.
findings.truth: This paper has no 9-mark item. It is ten questions over 100 marks, with extended open response at 6 marks. Both retyped as 6 marks.
findings.evidence: spec Paper 2 assessment information: ten questions, 100 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, multiple choice, short answer, calculations and extended open response

findings.claim: The match item offers 'Increases' twice on the right-hand side (boiling point and viscosity).
findings.truth: Two identical options in a match item can mark a correct pairing wrong, because the student may pick the other copy. The three options are now distinct while the pairing stays the same.

findings.claim: Two flashcard questions read 'What is the answer to: General formula for alkanes.'
findings.truth: Generated stem left in place. Rewritten as plain questions; the answers are unchanged and correct.

findings.claim: Ion charges are written as Li&sup+;, Ca&sup2+;, Fe&sup3+; and so on, eleven times.
findings.truth: '&sup+;' is not an HTML entity at all and '&sup2+;' is not one either, so the charges render as broken text on the page. Replaced with <sup> tags, which is what the rest of the unit uses.
findings.evidence: HTML entity list: ² and ³ exist, &sup+; does not; 11 occurrences, all in L4

findings.claim: The copper flame test colour is given as 'green' in the ion list, the key fact box, the conclusion and a flashcard.
findings.truth: The specification gives the copper flame colour as blue-green. The lesson contradicts itself: its own exam-focus paragraph already says 'copper gives blue-green'. All four places corrected.

findings.claim: Three higher-only wrappers cover the flame tests, the sodium hydroxide tests with the ammonium test, and the flame photometer.
findings.truth: None of 9.2C, 9.3C, 9.4C, 9.8C or 9.9C is bold. Same build fault as L2: separate-science content marked as Higher tier. All three wrappers removed.

findings.claim: A flashcard question reads 'What does Name three greenhouse gases state?'
findings.truth: The generated stem is broken text. Rewritten as 'What are three greenhouse gases?'; the answer is unchanged and correct.

findings.claim: The whole article is wrapped in a higher-only block and the lesson tier is 'higher'.
findings.truth: Alkenes and the bromine water test (9.10C-9.16C), addition polymers (9.17C-9.21C), the problems and recycling of polymers (9.23C, 9.24C), alcohols, the alcohol combustion core practical, fermentation and carboxylic acids (9.26C-9.34C) are none of them bold. Wrapper removed; see A2 for the tier field.

findings.claim: Condensation polymerisation was inside the blanket wrapper, so it lost its tier signal when the wrapper came off.
findings.truth: Condensation polymerisation appears in this specification only at 9.22C, which is bold, so it is genuinely Higher tier only. A narrow wrapper now covers that section, and the practice question, knowledge check and flashcard that test it are tagged (Higher tier).

findings.claim: The lesson teaches polyamides and nylon, esters made from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol, and ethanol made by hydration of ethene.
findings.truth: None of the three is in this specification. 'Polyamide', 'nylon', 'amide' and 'steam' do not appear anywhere in it; 'ester' appears only inside 9.22C, as the ester link in a polyester; ethanol production is fermentation only (9.33C, 9.34C). The chemistry is correct, so each is labelled as background rather than deleted. Two flashcards (nylon, and the product of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol) still test the out-of-scope material and are left as they are.
findings.evidence: grep of chemistry-1CH0-bold.md: no hits for polyamide, nylon, amide, hydration or steam

findings.claim: In L6, L7 and L8 the fifth knowledge check is a match item whose left column is truncated copies of the four questions above it, ending in '...', with those questions' answers on the right.
findings.truth: It is an auto-generated placeholder: it teaches nothing new, shows cut-off text, and duplicates the lesson's own questions. Each one rebuilt as a real four-pair match on that lesson's content, with distinct right-hand options and the pairing checked.
findings.evidence: placeholder check; left entries such as 'small molecule is released when two monomers jo...'

findings.claim: The whole article is wrapped in a higher-only block and the lesson tier is 'higher'.
findings.truth: Nanoparticle size and surface area to volume ratio, their uses and risks, and the comparison of glass, ceramics, polymers, composites and metals (9.35C-9.39C) contain no bold text at all. Wrapper removed; see A2 for the tier field.

findings.claim: The lesson teaches reverse osmosis as a desalination method and a four-stage sewage works ending in anaerobic digestion and biogas.
findings.truth: Neither is in this specification. 2.12b names distillation as the way to make sea water potable, and 2.12a asks only for sedimentation, filtration and chlorination. Both passages labelled as background rather than deleted.
findings.evidence: spec 2.12a, 2.12b; no spec hits for reverse osmosis, screening, sludge or biogas

findings.claim: 'Thermal cracking (steam cracking): carried out at very high temperatures (around 850 degrees C) and high pressure using steam.'
findings.truth: Thermal cracking and steam cracking are conflated; steam cracking dilutes with steam and runs at low pressure, which is the opposite of high pressure. Neither is required: 8.16 and 8.17 ask only what cracking does and why it is needed. Not corrected, because the fix would ripple through the exam-focus paragraph as well and no mark depends on it.

findings.claim: Chlorine test: 'hold damp litmus paper in the gas - it is first turned red (acid) then bleached white.'
findings.truth: The red-then-bleach sequence only happens with damp BLUE litmus. The bleaching is the mark point and is right, so no edit; a future pass could add the word 'blue'.
findings.evidence: spec 6.8 describes the chemical test for chlorine without naming the litmus colour

findings.claim: Fine particles are given as 100-2500 nm, and soda glass and borosilicate glass are compared in detail.
findings.truth: Both are AQA framing. 1CH0 asks only that students compare the physical properties of glass, clay ceramics, polymers, composites and metals using data (9.38C), and does not name glass types or particle size bands. The content is correct, so it is recorded rather than edited.

findings.claim: Exam-tip paragraphs sit at the end of content_html in L1 (n30), L3 (n38 and n39) and L4 (n42), duplicating the job of exam_tip_html.
findings.truth: No exam_tip_html field in this unit is truncated; the fault runs the other way. Recorded only, because the brief says not to move text between fields.
findings.evidence: structural check of all eight lessons

findings.claim: Haber yields given as 'around 98% at room temperature' and 'around 15-25%' at 450 degrees C and 200 atmospheres.
findings.truth: Neither figure is in the specification and textbooks quote anything from 15% to 28% for the 450 degrees C / 200 atm case. The figures are plausible and no mark depends on them, so they are left.
findings.evidence: spec 4.16 gives the conditions only, not the yield

summary: Eight lessons checked against 1CH0 and its bold-preserved twin. Two HIGH science or answer-key errors (copper flame colour given as green when the spec says blue-green, in four places; a match item with two identical options). The dominant fault is the known higher-only wrapper misuse: six wrappers across L2, L4, L6 and L7 covered content that is not bold, and only 4.17, 5.20C, 5.21C and 9.22C are genuinely Higher tier. L1 and L5 carry no science errors. The unit-level problem is mapping: L2, L8 and the chromatography half of L4 are Paper 1 content, and topic 6 and the energy half of topic 7 are missing entirely (A1). 68 edits, all verified unique against the raw fields, with div balance and narration-id counts unchanged.
